mainTopic: Liver and blood: cooking liver with other meat, draining its blood, and roasting liver or udder above other meat
overview: The גמרא finishes an earlier question by saying the other food was forbidden because of the liver's fat. It then asks a new question: does the liver's blood make other meat cooked with it forbidden? רבי זריקא brings a story where rabbis ate a windpipe cooked with the liver, but רב אשי rejects the proof, so the question has no answer from that story. A side point follows: רבא shows that vinegar used to scald liver cannot be forbidden. Next, רב נחמן insists that his guest eat cooked liver, and the גמרא shows that תנאים already argued about liver cooked with other meat. A story at a שבת meal teaches how to cut liver so the blood in its vessels drains out, and the גמרא adds that spleen, which is just fat, needs no cutting. Then come two opposite versions of a rule about roasting liver or udder above other meat, and מרימר gives the final הלכה. The amud ends as a new story about רב אשי at his father-in-law's house begins, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The earlier case is forbidden because of fat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wraps up the previous question: the other food was forbidden because of the liver's fat, not its blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is forbidden because of the fat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is closing off the earlier question. The food was forbidden because it soaked up fat (שמנוניתא) from the liver.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this line, אביי wanted to know why food cooked with forbidden liver becomes forbidden: is it blood or fat? This line gives the answer: fat. That leaves the blood question open for the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Fat or greasiness absorbed from meat
Liver, which is full of blood

phrases.english: And it is because of the fat.
phrases.notes: This finishes the answer from רבי זריקא's first conversation: the liver's fat is what made the other food forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the inquiry carried over from the previous section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The prohibition in the earlier case came from absorbed fat, not blood.

steps.title: What about the liver's blood alone?
steps.stepSummary: New question: if permitted liver is cooked with other meat, does the liver's blood make that meat forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: If the only concern is blood, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question. If the only worry is the blood coming out of the liver, is the other meat forbidden?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fat soaks into other food easily, so that case was clear. Blood might behave differently and soak in less. So the גמרא asks about blood separately.

phrases.english: Because of blood, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Picture kosher liver cooked with other meat. The only question is whether its blood seeps into that meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the fat answer and asks about the remaining factor, blood.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether blood released from liver forbids other meat cooked with it.

steps.title: רבי זריקא answers from a meal he ate
steps.stepSummary: רבי זריקא says he ate a windpipe cooked together with the liver and other organs, so blood from liver does not make other meat forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב ספרא went up again, he met רבי זריקא. רבי זריקא said: You don't need to ask this either. ינאי the son of רבי אמי and I visited the house of יהודה the son of רבי שמעון בן פזי. They served us the windpipe with all its attached organs, and we ate it.
steps.whatsHappening: On his next trip to ארץ ישראל, רב ספרא puts the question to רבי זריקא. רבי זריקא answers with a real story about what he and others ate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The windpipe was cooked still attached to the lungs, heart and liver. Great rabbis ate it, which seems to show that the liver's blood did not make the other organs forbidden. This proof comes from what people actually did, not from a teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: You need not ask (the answer is clear)

phrases.english: When he again went up,
phrases.notes: This is רב ספרא, going up to ארץ ישראל again.

phrases.english: he found Rabbi Zerika,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַאי נָמֵי לָא תִּבְּעֵי לָךְ,
phrases.english: he said to him: this too you need not ask,
for I and Yannai son of Rabbi Ami
happened to come to the house of Yehuda son of
Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi,
and they brought us the windpipe with its attachments,
and we ate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the blood question with a story of what was done in practice.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Liver's blood does not forbid other meat, since organs cooked with the liver were eaten.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A meal at the house of יהודה בן רבי שמעון בן פזי

steps.title: רב אשי says the story proves nothing
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects the proof: maybe the blood drained out of the pot, or maybe the liver was scalded first, the way רב הונא and רב נחמן did it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי, and some say רבי שמואל from זרוקיניא, objected: Maybe the open end of the windpipe was outside the pot. Or maybe they scalded the liver at the start, the way רב הונא had it scalded in vinegar and רב נחמן had it scalded in boiling water.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back on רבי זריקא's story. He gives two other reasons why that meal may have been fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason one: if the windpipe's opening hung outside the pot, the blood would flow out and not reach the other organs. Reason two: scalding the liver first seals its blood inside. Either way, the story does not prove that blood in a normal case is harmless, so the question stays open.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying blood forbids other meat. He is only saying that this story cannot prove that it doesn't. The question is still unanswered.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi objects,
and some say Rabbi Shmuel from Zerukinya:

phrases.aramaic: וְדִלְמָא פִּי קָנֶה חוּץ לִקְדֵרָה הֲוָה,
phrases.english: but perhaps the mouth of the windpipe was outside the pot,
phrases.notes: Then the blood would drain out through the windpipe instead of soaking into the other organs.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי מִיחְלָט הֲוָה חָלֵיט לֵיהּ מֵעִיקָּרָא,
phrases.english: alternatively, he had scalded it at the outset,
like that of Rav Huna:
they would scald it for him in vinegar,
and Rav Nachman, they would scald it for him in boiling water.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אָשֵׁי, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל מִזְּרוּקִינְיָא: וְדִלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the story. It makes no ruling on the blood question itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The story may have had special conditions (blood draining out, or liver scalded first) that kept the blood from spreading.
steps.whatToRemember: The question about liver's blood is left unresolved, because the story can be explained by special conditions.

steps.title: רב פפא thinks the scalding vinegar becomes forbidden
steps.stepSummary: While learning before רבא, רב פפא wanted to say that vinegar used to scald liver becomes forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא, sitting before רבא, thought to say: the vinegar is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a side point that comes from רב הונא's vinegar. רב פפא suggests that the vinegar soaks up blood and becomes forbidden, which sets up רבא's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא assumes the liver gives off blood into the hot vinegar. If so, the vinegar would now contain blood and be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Thought to say (a first idea that may be rejected)

phrases.aramaic: וּסְבַר רַב פָּפָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא לְמֵימַר:
phrases.english: And Rav Pappa thought, before Rava, to say:
the vinegar is forbidden.
phrases.notes: This is the vinegar used to scald the liver, like רב הונא's practice.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּסְבַר רַב פָּפָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the vinegar detail from רב הונא's practice in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפא's first idea: vinegar used to scald liver is forbidden.

steps.title: רבא: then the liver would be forbidden too
steps.stepSummary: רבא shows that if the vinegar were forbidden, the liver would be forbidden too, since it would absorb the blood back. So the vinegar must be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: If the vinegar is forbidden, then the liver is forbidden too, because just as it gives out blood, it soaks it back in.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects רב פפא's idea by showing where it leads. That ending is something nobody accepts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liver sitting in hot vinegar would both give off and take in. If blood went out into the vinegar, the liver would take that forbidden vinegar back in. Everyone agrees the scalded liver is permitted, so no blood is let out during scalding, and the vinegar is permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the rule that food cooking in liquid both gives off and takes in. That is why scalding liver keeps its blood sealed inside.
steps.whatToRemember: Scalding liver in vinegar does not make the vinegar forbidden. Otherwise the liver itself would be forbidden.

phrases.english: He said to him: if the vinegar is forbidden,
it too is forbidden,
for just as it expels, it then absorbs back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי חַלָּא אֲסִיר – אִיהוּ נָמֵי אֲסִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב פפא's suggestion in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects fully the idea that the scalding vinegar is forbidden.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It leads to a forbidden liver, because the liver would take back in whatever it gave out.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the vinegar is forbidden, the liver should be forbidden too, but scalded liver is permitted.

steps.title: רב בר שבא refuses cooked liver
steps.stepSummary: רב בר שבא would not eat cooked liver at רב נחמן's house. רב נחמן told his household to make him eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב בר שבא visited רב נחמן's house. They served him cooked liver, but he did not eat it. The household told רב נחמן, 'A Torah student inside is not eating.' 'Who is he?' 'רב בר שבא.' רב נחמן said, 'Make שבא eat it!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. A guest would not eat cooked liver, and his host, רב נחמן, insisted that the liver was fine to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב בר שבא was worried about the blood in the liver, so he would not eat liver that had been cooked. רב נחמן told them to feed it to him, which shows that רב נחמן held cooked liver is permitted. This fits the earlier step where רב נחמן's method of preparing liver was mentioned.

keyTerms.meaning: Liver that has been stewed or cooked in liquid
Stuff it in, make him eat

phrases.aramaic: רַב בַּר שְׁבָא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב נַחְמָן,
phrases.english: Rav bar Shaba happened to visit the house of Rav Nachman.
They brought him cooked liver,
and he did not eat it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: בַּר בֵּי רַב דִּלְגָיו לָא אָכֵיל,
phrases.english: They said to him: A Torah student inside is not eating.
phrases.notes: The household is speaking to רב נחמן, telling him about his guest.

phrases.english: And who is he? Rav bar Shaba.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב נַחְמָן: גַּאמוּ לְשַׁבָּא.
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to them: Stuff it into Shaba!
phrases.notes: He means: feed it to him even if he doesn't want it, because the liver is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב בַּר שְׁבָא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a story showing how רב נחמן himself treated cooked liver
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן held that cooked liver is permitted to eat

steps.title: The question about liver is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The question of liver cooked with other meat matches a dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches a dispute between תנאים. רבי אליעזר says: liver forbids other food but does not become forbidden itself, because it gives out blood but does not absorb it. רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says: if it is spiced, it forbids and becomes forbidden. If it is stewed, it forbids and becomes forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the question from step 2 was already argued about by תנאים. That question asked whether the liver's blood forbids other meat cooked with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר says that liver cooked with other meat always forbids that meat, because its blood comes out, but the liver itself stays permitted. רבי ישמעאל mentions only liver that is spiced or stewed, which forbids the meat and also becomes forbidden itself. That suggests that ordinary cooked liver does not cause a problem at all, so the two תנאים disagree about the very question from step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: This is like a dispute between תנאים
It forbids other food but does not become forbidden itself
It gives out liquid but does not absorb it
Stewed, cooked a long time in liquid

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: liver always forbids the meat cooked with it, but the liver itself is not forbidden. רבי ישמעאל: only spiced or stewed liver forbids the other meat, and then the liver is forbidden too.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two directions. 'אוסרת' means the liver makes other food forbidden. 'נאסרת' means the liver itself becomes forbidden.

phrases.english: This is like a dispute between תנאים:
phrases.notes: This goes back to the question in step 2, about liver cooked with other meat.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: הַכָּבֵד אוֹסֶרֶת וְאֵינָהּ נֶאֱסֶרֶת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: The liver forbids other food but is not forbidden itself,
because it gives out blood but does not absorb it.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, says:
If it is spiced, it forbids other food and is forbidden itself;
if it is stewed, it forbids other food and is forbidden itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the question from step 2 and shows that תנאים already argued about it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: liver forbids but is not forbidden. רבי ישמעאל: spiced or stewed liver forbids and is forbidden.

steps.title: A special meal in honor of שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא is served fancy bread and asks whether it was made for him. The hosts answer that it was made in honor of שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא visited the house of רבה בר רב נחמן. They put three סאה of fine kneaded bread in front of him. He asked, 'Did you know I was coming?' They answered, 'Are you more important to us than שבת? It is written, "And you shall call שבת a delight"!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story. This part sets the scene for the next steps, where a problem with a liver comes up during the same meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The guest assumed the fancy food was made in his honor. The hosts explain that they make such food every week to honor שבת, based on the פסוק. This step is mostly background for the liver episode that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Fine bread or cakes, kneaded with rich ingredients

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אִקְּלַע לְבֵי רַבָּה בַּר רַב נַחְמָן,
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna happened to visit the house of Rabba bar Rav Nachman.
They brought before him three se'ah of fine kneaded bread.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: מִי הֲוָה יָדְעִיתוּ דְּאָתֵינָא?
phrases.english: He said to them: Did you know that I was coming?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: מִי עֲדִיפַתְּ לַן מִינַּהּ,
phrases.english: They said to him: Are you more important to us than it,
phrases.notes: 'It' means שבת. The visit took place on שבת.

phrases.english: as it is written: "And you shall call שבת a delight"!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אִקְּלַע לְבֵי רַבָּה בַּר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story that will lead into a practical rule about preparing liver
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fancy food is prepared every week in honor of שבת, as a fulfillment of עונג שבת

steps.title: A liver with a blood-filled vessel
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא finds a liver with a blood vessel still full of blood and objects to how it was prepared.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile, he found a liver that had a blood vessel with blood soaked inside it. He said to them, 'Why did you do this?'
steps.whatsHappening: During the meal, the guest sees that the liver still has blood trapped in one of its vessels, and he challenges his hosts about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not the liver itself, which the גמרא has treated as allowed. The problem is the blood collected inside the blood vessel, which did not drain out. His question 'why did you do this?' is really a complaint that the liver was prepared wrongly.

keyTerms.meaning: A blood vessel or tube inside the liver

phrases.english: Meanwhile, he found a certain liver
that had in it a blood vessel soaked with blood.
He said to them: Why did you do it this way?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same meal story with a problem about the liver
steps.kashyaTarget: The way the hosts prepared the liver
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blood trapped in the liver's blood vessel was left inside, so the liver was not prepared properly

steps.title: How to prepare liver so the blood drains
steps.stepSummary: The hosts ask how they should prepare liver. רבה בר רב הונא tells them to cut it lengthwise and crosswise and put the cut side down.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him, 'So how should we do it?' He told them, 'Tear it lengthwise and widthwise, and place the cut side facing down.'
steps.whatsHappening: The hosts ask for the correct method, and the guest gives practical instructions for preparing liver.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting the liver in both directions opens up the blood vessels. Placing the cut side down lets the blood flow out instead of staying inside. This answers the problem raised in the previous step.

keyTerms.meaning: Lengthwise and widthwise, like threads in a woven cloth

steps.whatToRemember: Liver must be cut open in both directions and placed cut side down, so that the blood trapped in its blood vessels can drain out.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a practical method for preparing liver so that forbidden blood in its vessels comes out.

phrases.english: They said to him: Rather, how should we do it?
He said to them: Tear it lengthwise and widthwise,
and put the cut side downward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 10 with the correct method
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How liver should be prepared so that no blood remains in its blood vessels
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Cut it lengthwise and widthwise and place the cut side down

steps.title: The cutting rule applies to liver, not spleen
steps.stepSummary: The rule of cutting the liver open applies only to liver. Spleen is just fat and does not need it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only to liver. But spleen is just fat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the rule from step 11. Only liver needs to be cut open; spleen does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liver has blood vessels full of blood, so it must be cut lengthwise and crosswise for the blood to drain. Spleen is treated as fat, not as a blood-filled organ, so no cutting is needed. This is a limit on the rule, not a new topic.

keyTerms.meaning: And this rule applies only to

phrases.english: And this applies to liver,
phrases.notes: "This" is רבה בר רב הונא's rule from step 11: cut the liver lengthwise and crosswise and put it cut side down.

phrases.english: but spleen
is merely fat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the liver-cutting instruction of step 11 so that it does not cover spleen.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only liver needs to be cut open for its blood to drain. Spleen is treated as fat and needs no special cutting.

steps.title: Support from שמואל's spleen dish
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's household cooked a dish of spleens for him on the day of his bloodletting, which shows spleen is treated as ordinary food.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like the story of שמואל: they used to make him a dish of spleens on the day he had bloodletting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the previous step with a story about שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They cooked spleen for שמואל as an ordinary dish and did nothing special to drain blood. This fits the idea that spleen is just fat and not a blood problem.

phrases.english: Like that story about Shmuel:
they would make him a dish of spleens
on the day he did "the thing."
phrases.notes: "The thing" is a polite way of saying bloodletting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 12's claim that spleen is only fat.
steps.raayaObject: Spleen does not need the special cutting that liver needs.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's household regularly cooked spleens for him on his bloodletting day.

steps.title: Liver above meat is permitted, udder above meat is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: If liver is above other meat while they roast, the meat is permitted because blood slides off. If udder is above the meat, the meat is forbidden because the milk sticks to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: liver on top of meat is permitted, because the blood just slides off. Udder on top of meat is forbidden. Why? The milk sticks to the meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about roasting liver or udder above other meat. It rules differently for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both liver and udder drip something onto the meat below: blood from the liver, milk from the udder. The difference is how it behaves. Blood slides off without soaking in, but milk is sticky and gets absorbed, so the meat becomes forbidden.

phrases.english: It was stated: liver on top of meat
phrases.notes: The case is meat being roasted together, with one piece hanging above the other so its juices drip down.

phrases.english: is permitted, because the blood slides right off.
Udder on top of meat is forbidden.
What is the reason?
The milk sticks and clings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from preparing liver on its own to roasting liver or udder together with other meat.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liver above meat: the meat is permitted. Udder above meat: the meat is forbidden, because milk is absorbed and blood is not.

steps.title: רב דימי teaches the opposite
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי מנהרדעא reverses the rulings. Udder above meat is permitted because the milk of a slaughtered animal is only forbidden מדרבנן. Liver above meat is forbidden because blood is forbidden מדאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי from נהרדעא taught it the other way around: udder on top of meat is permitted. Why? The milk of a slaughtered animal is only a rabbinic prohibition. Liver on top of meat is forbidden, because blood is a Torah prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי gives a different version of the teaching, with the two rulings flipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version decided based on how the liquid behaves (sliding versus sticking). רב דימי decides based on how serious each prohibition is. Milk from an udder of a slaughtered animal is only forbidden מדרבנן, so we can be lenient. Blood is forbidden מדאורייתא, so we must be strict.

keyTerms.meaning: Milk in the udder of a slaughtered animal

steps.confusionAlert: Here "חלב" is read חָלָב, meaning milk. It is not חֵלֶב, forbidden fat. The topic is milk dripping from the udder onto meat.

phrases.english: Rav Dimi from Neharde'a taught the opposite:
udder on top of meat is permitted.
What is the reason? The milk of a slaughtered animal is rabbinic.
Liver on top of meat is forbidden,
because blood is a Torah prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reverse version of step 14's rulings, based on a different reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Udder above meat: the meat is permitted, since the milk is only rabbinic. Liver above meat: the meat is forbidden, since blood is a Torah prohibition.

steps.title: מרימר's final ruling
steps.stepSummary: מרימר rules that liver or udder underneath the meat is permitted. On top of the meat, it is permitted after the fact but should not be done to begin with.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר taught: the הלכה is that whether it is liver or udder, below the meat it is permitted. Above the meat, after the fact it is permitted, but you should not do it from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: מרימר gives the final הלכה, treating liver and udder the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not pick one version over the other. Instead, he combines them into one practical rule. Below the meat, nothing drips onto it, so both are fully permitted. Above the meat, because of the doubt from the two versions, one should avoid it לכתחילה, but if it already happened the meat is not forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, before doing it

steps.whatToRemember: Liver or udder below meat: permitted. Above meat: avoid it לכתחילה, but the meat is permitted בדיעבד.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling settles the dispute between the two versions with a practical rule for roasting liver or udder together with other meat.

phrases.english: Mareimar taught publicly: the halacha is,
whether liver or udder,
underneath the meat, it is permitted;
on top of the meat,
after the fact, yes; from the start, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the dispute between steps 14 and 15 with one rule for both liver and udder.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Liver or udder below the meat is permitted. Above the meat, the meat is permitted after the fact, but one should not roast them that way to begin with.

steps.title: רב אשי visits his father-in-law's house
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a story. רב אשי came to the house of his father-in-law רמי בר אבא and saw something that רמי בר אבא's son was doing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי came to the house of his father-in-law, רמי בר אבא. He saw that the son of רמי בר אבא was...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a story and setting the scene for the next move. We have not yet been told what the son was doing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only introduces the people and the place: רב אשי is visiting his father-in-law's house. The story about what the son was doing continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: happened to come / arrived at (a place)
that he was (doing something), describing an action in progress

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence stops in the middle. Do not try to finish the story from this line. What the son was doing is told in the words that come next.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi arrived
at the house of Rami bar Abba, his father-in-law,
he saw the son
of Rami bar Abba, that he was

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רָמֵי בַּר אַבָּא חֲמוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new story about a practice רב אשי saw at his father-in-law's house; the story continues on the next amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This line only sets the scene: רב אשי is at רמי בר אבא's house and watches what the son is doing.
